Key Finding: Structured work-integrated learning strengthens student employability skills, though inconsistent supervision and unclear task expectations can hinder workplace learning outcomes.
APA Reference: Jackson, D. (2015). Employability skill development in work-integrated learning: Barriers and best practice. *Studies in Higher Education*, *40*(2), 350–367. https://doi.org/10.1080/03075079.2013.842221

Key Finding: Higher education students rarely produce deep critical reflections spontaneously and require structured scaffolding to connect practical experiences with academic learning.
APA Reference: Ryan, M. (2013). The pedagogical balancing act: Teaching reflection in higher education. *Teaching in Higher Education*, *18*(2), 144–155. https://doi.org/10.1080/13562517.2012.694104

Key Finding: Students using unguarded generative AI tools perform worse on subsequent unassisted assessments than peers without AI, whereas scaffolded guardrails prevent this learning loss.
APA Reference: Bastani, H., Bastani, O., Sungu, A., Ge, H., Kabakcı, Ö., & Mariman, R. (2025). Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning: Evidence from high school mathematics. *PNAS*, *122*(26), e2422633122. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2422633122

Key Finding: Progressive web apps bridge traditional web and native mobile capabilities through a single codebase, offering offline support and home-screen installation across devices.
APA Reference: Majchrzak, T. A., Biørn-Hansen, A., & Grønli, T.-M. (2018). Progressive web apps: The definite approach to cross-platform development? *Proceedings of the 51st Hawaii International Conference on System Sciences*, 5735–5744. https://doi.org/10.24251/HICSS.2018.718

Key Finding: Neural natural language generation models frequently produce fluent text that contradicts or cannot be verified against source inputs, creating factual reliability risks.
APA Reference: Ji, Z., Lee, N., Frieske, R., Yu, T., Su, D., Xu, Y., Ishii, E., Bang, Y., Madotto, A., & Fung, P. (2023). Survey of hallucination in natural language generation. *ACM Computing Surveys*, *55*(12), 1–38. https://doi.org/10.1145/3571730

Key Finding: Commercial AI text detectors frequently misclassify human-written essays by non-native English writers as AI-generated, making automated detection unreliable for verifying authorship.
APA Reference: Liang, W., Yuksekgonul, M., Mao, Y., Wu, E., & Zou, J. (2023). GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers. *Patterns*, *4*(7), 100779. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patter.2023.100779

Key Finding: Access to generative AI reduces professional writing task completion time by 40 percent and raises output quality by 18 percent, with the largest gains among lower-skill writers.
APA Reference: Noy, S., & Zhang, W. (2023). Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence. *Science*, *381*(6654), 187–192. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adh2586

Key Finding: Large language models integrated with complementary software tools can accelerate roughly half of workforce tasks, exposing higher-education and knowledge occupations to rapid change.
APA Reference: Eloundou, T., Manning, S., Mishkin, P., & Rock, D. (2024). GPTs are GPTs: Labor market impact potential of LLMs. *Science*, *384*(6702), 1306–1308. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adj0998

Key Finding: Integrating structured internships into higher education degree programs significantly improves graduate employability and shortens the transition from university to paid employment.
APA Reference: Silva, P., Lopes, B., Costa, M., Melo, A. I., Dias, G. P., Brito, E., & Seabra, D. (2018). The million-dollar question: Can internships boost employment? *Studies in Higher Education*, *43*(1), 2–21. https://doi.org/10.1080/03075079.2016.1144181

Key Finding: Training and tuning large neural language models consumes substantial electricity and generates high carbon emissions, prompting calls for more computationally efficient model choices.
APA Reference: Strubell, E., Ganesh, A., & McCallum, A. (2019). Energy and policy considerations for deep learning in NLP. *Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics*, 3645–3650. https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/P19-1355

Key Finding: General-purpose generative AI models consume orders of magnitude more energy per inference than smaller task-specific models, creating significant cumulative operational carbon costs.
APA Reference: Luccioni, A. S., Jernite, Y., & Strubell, E. (2024). Power hungry processing: Watts driving the cost of AI deployment? *Proceedings of the 2024 ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency*, 85–99. https://doi.org/10.1145/3630106.3658542

Key Finding: Global data centre electricity consumption is projected to more than double by 2030 to around 945 terawatt-hours, driven primarily by expanding artificial intelligence workloads.
APA Reference: International Energy Agency. (2024). *Electricity 2024: Analysis and forecast to 2026*. IEA. https://www.iea.org/reports/electricity-2024

Key Finding: Educational institutions should validate generative AI tools for ethical and pedagogical fitness, enforce data privacy safeguards, and keep human agency central in learning.
APA Reference: Miao, F., & Holmes, W. (2023). *Guidance for generative AI in education and research*. UNESCO. https://doi.org/10.54675/EWZM9535

Key Finding: Philippine higher education institutions must formally monitor student interns, verify required training hours, and evaluate practicum performance alongside host establishments.
APA Reference: Commission on Higher Education. (2017). *Revised guidelines for student internship program in the Philippines (SIPP) for all programs* (CHED Memorandum Order No. 104, s. 2017). https://www.ched.gov.ph

Key Finding: Intergovernmental AI governance principles require transparency when users interact with AI systems, robust information integrity safeguards, and clear accountability across lifecycles.
APA Reference: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. (2024). *Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence* (OECD/LEGAL/0449). https://legalinstruments.oecd.org/en/instruments/oecd-legal-0449

Key Finding: Philippine data privacy law classifies student educational records as sensitive personal information, requiring explicit consent and strict technical security controls against unauthorized access.
APA Reference: *Data Privacy Act of 2012*, Rep. Act No. 10173 (Phil.). https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2012/08/15/republic-act-no-10173/

Key Finding: European AI legislation classifies systems used to evaluate educational learning outcomes as high-risk, mandating strict data governance, transparency, and human oversight obligations.
APA Reference: *Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council (Artificial Intelligence Act)*, 2024 O.J. (L 2024/1689). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj

Key Finding: Philippine copyright law automatically protects original student literary works from creation and grants authors inalienable moral rights of attribution and integrity over modifications.
APA Reference: *Intellectual Property Code of the Philippines*, Rep. Act No. 8293 (Phil.). https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1997/06/06/republic-act-no-8293/

Key Finding: Universities cannot rely solely on AI detection tools to police academic dishonesty and should instead prioritize transparent, process-oriented assessments and ethical AI literacy.
APA Reference: Cotton, D. R. E., Cotton, P. A., & Shipway, J. R. (2024). Chatting and cheating: Ensuring academic integrity in the era of ChatGPT. *Innovations in Education and Teaching International*, *61*(2), 228–239. https://doi.org/10.1080/14703297.2023.2190148

Key Finding: Maintaining academic integrity with large language models requires clear institutional boundaries between acceptable writing assistance and unauthorized content generation.
APA Reference: Perkins, M. (2023). Academic integrity considerations of AI large language models in the post-pandemic era: ChatGPT and beyond. *Journal of University Teaching & Learning Practice*, *20*(2), Article 7. https://doi.org/10.53761/1.20.02.07

Key Finding: Collecting and storing student activity data raises ethical dilemmas around informed consent, surveillance, and data stewardship that require transparent student-centered governance.
APA Reference: Slade, S., & Prinsloo, P. (2013). Learning analytics: Ethical issues and dilemmas. *American Behavioral Scientist*, *57*(10), 1510–1529. https://doi.org/10.1177/0002764213479366
